covers.quote: To make sure screen readers read the minus symbol, use the mathematical symbol for minus.

rules.quote: Don’t use an en dash instead of a minus symbol.
rules.violation_condition: An en dash is used to mean mathematical minus rather than the mathematical minus symbol.
when: Applies when the symbol represents mathematical minus.
rules.why: G-4: the positive instruction to use the mathematical minus symbol restates the prohibition.

rules.quote: Use the entity – in HTML.
rules.violation_condition: An en dash in HTML is represented without the prescribed – entity.
when: Applies to HTML source containing an en dash.
rules.why: This is a distinct instruction about the textual representation of an en dash in HTML.

rules.quote: Use the entity − in HTML.
rules.violation_condition: A mathematical minus symbol in HTML is represented without the prescribed − entity.
when: Applies to HTML source containing a mathematical minus symbol.
rules.why: The HTML representation is a separate check from whether the symbol means minus.

rules.quote: Don’t confuse the dash or the minus symbol for a hyphen.
rules.specification: Interpret this as a prohibition on substituting a dash or minus symbol for a word-joining hyphen, not as a prohibition on valid coordinate-noun en dashes.
rules.violation_condition: An en dash, em dash or mathematical minus symbol is used where a hyphen is required.
when: Applies where the intended function is that of a hyphen.
rules.why: The instruction concerns symbol substitution; its wording needs an operational interpretation.

covers.quote: Avoid using en dashes in most content.
That is why, in general content, it’s better to use phrases for most spans of numbers.
You can use en dashes in technical content, particularly if it contains a lot of spans.
Instead, use the phrases:
‘from’ paired with ‘to’ – for example, ‘from 57 to 65 years’
‘between’ paired with ‘and’ – for example, ‘between Monday and Friday’.
Use en dashes for date spans in:
financial years
calendar years
the titles of publications and programs
terms of office
lifespans (birth and death)
limited space.
Date spans in headings should follow the general rule, except when:
the heading contains a title that has an en dash
using words would push the character count over 70 characters (including spaces).
Only use en dashes for time spans when you have limited space.
Using en dashes for date spans is allowed when you have limited space.
Restrict the use of an en dash for a date span in headings
Only use en dashes for date spans in headings when:
your heading includes a title that contains en dashes
using words pushes the character count above 70 characters (including spaces).
In all other cases, write date spans in headings with words.
Use the phrases ‘from … to’ and ‘between … and’.
Only use an en dash for a time span when space is limited
Use en dashes for time spans only when you have limited space.
In technical content where there are many numbers, you can use en dashes for number, date and page spans.

rules.quote: Avoid using en dashes for spans in body text and headings.
rules.specification: The distinction between general and technical content, and what counts as limited space outside the explicit heading threshold, requires contextual judgement.
rules.violation_condition: An en dash expresses a span in general-content body text or a heading outside the stated exceptions.
when: Use phrases such as ‘from … to’ and ‘between … and’ for ordinary spans in general content.
Date-span exceptions cover financial years, calendar years, publication and program titles, terms of office, lifespans, and limited space.
For headings, an en dash is allowed when the heading contains a title with an en dash or wording the span would push the heading above 70 characters including spaces.
Time spans may use en dashes only when space is limited.
Technical content containing many spans may use en dashes.
rules.why: G-2 and G-3: the restrictions and permissions change when the same span-avoidance check applies, rather than creating repeated findings.

covers.quote: Don’t combine en dashes with ‘from’ or ‘to’ in the spans.

rules.quote: Never mix ‘from’ or ‘between’ with an en dash.
rules.violation_condition: A span combines ‘from’ or ‘between’ with an en dash, or a technical-content span combines ‘to’ with an en dash.
when: The word and dash must belong to the same span, not merely occur near each other.
The technical-content instruction additionally prohibits combining ‘to’ with an en dash.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: the technical-content wording adds a case to the same mixed-span construction check.

covers.quote: Use an en dash for a financial year
Join them with an unspaced en dash.
For financial years that cross centuries, use 4 digits on either side of the en dash.

rules.quote: For financial years, use 4 digits for the first number and only 2 digits for the second.
rules.violation_condition: A financial-year span is not written with a 4-digit starting year and 2-digit ending year joined by an unspaced en dash, or uses a shortened ending year when crossing centuries.
when: For financial years crossing centuries, use 4 digits for both years.
The span uses an unspaced en dash.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: crossing centuries changes the required form of the same financial-year span.

rules.quote: Use the phrases ‘financial year’ and ‘financial years’ at first mention, unless the context makes the meaning clear.
rules.specification: Whether the context already makes the financial-year meaning clear requires judgement.
rules.violation_condition: The first mention of a financial year lacks ‘financial year’ or ‘financial years’ and the context does not make the meaning clear.
when: Applies at first mention.
The phrase is unnecessary when context makes the meaning clear.
rules.why: This checks first-mention explanation, not the financial-year span’s numerical form.

covers.quote: Use an en dash for a calendar year
Join them with an unspaced en dash.

rules.quote: For calendar years, use 4 digits for the first number and either 4 or 2 digits for the second number.
rules.violation_condition: A calendar-year span lacks a 4-digit starting year, has an ending year of neither 2 nor 4 digits, or is not joined by an unspaced en dash.
when: Applies to calendar-year spans.
rules.why: G-4: the body gives the actionable calendar-year format and absorbs its heading.

rules.quote: Use the phrases ‘calendar year’ and ‘calendar years’ at first mention, unless the context makes the meaning clear.
rules.specification: Whether the context already makes the calendar-year meaning clear requires judgement.
rules.violation_condition: The first mention of calendar years lacks ‘calendar year’ or ‘calendar years’ and the context does not make the meaning clear.
when: Applies at first mention.
The phrase is unnecessary when context makes the meaning clear.
rules.why: This is a first-mention explanation check, separate from numerical formatting.

covers.quote: Use an en dash for a date span in titles of publications and programs
If you cross the century, always use 4 digits for both years.
Use 4 digits on both sides of the span for these titles if that is your organisation’s house style.

rules.quote: When you create a title, use 4 digits for the first year and 2 digits for the second year.
rules.violation_condition: A newly created publication or program title uses a year span without an en dash or with year lengths other than the prescribed 4-digit start and 2-digit end, subject to the century and house-style exceptions.
when: Applies when creating a publication or program title.
A span crossing a century always uses 4 digits for both years.
An organisation’s house style may require 4 digits on both sides.
Titles created by other people or organisations retain their original year-span style.
rules.why: G-2 to G-4: century and house-style cases modify one title-creation formatting check.

covers.quote: Reproduce titles with en dashes when you cite them as a reference.

rules.quote: When you refer to a title published by another person or organisation, retain the style that was originally used for year spans.
rules.violation_condition: A reference to a published title changes its original year-span style, including replacing an original en dash.
when: Applies when referring to another person’s or organisation’s published title.
Also applies when reproducing a title as a reference.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: citations are another case of preserving the published title’s span style.

covers.quote: Use an en dash for a term of office

rules.quote: Always use 4 digits for both dates, joined by an unspaced en dash.
rules.violation_condition: A term-of-office year span has a shortened year or is not joined by an unspaced en dash.
when: Applies to a person’s term of office.
rules.why: G-4: the body supplies the full requirement; ‘usually’ does not make parentheses mandatory.

covers.quote: Use an en dash for a person’s lifespan

rules.quote: Always use 4 digits for both dates, joined by an unspaced en dash.
rules.violation_condition: A person’s birth-to-death year span has a shortened year or is not joined by an unspaced en dash.
when: Applies to a person’s lifespan.
rules.why: G-4: the body specifies the lifespan format without requiring its usual parenthetical placement.

covers.quote: Use the following style for en dashes in spans of days and months:
The en dash is unspaced when the month only appears at the end of the span.

rules.quote: The en dash is spaced when the day and month appear on both sides of the span.
